# FreeSpace 2 campaign mission reconstruction reference

> A clean-room, implementation-oriented index of the complete retail single-player campaign structure: 30 main story missions, five optional SOC-loop missions and six training missions. Mission mechanics are retained exactly from the extracted FRED data; long briefing, debriefing and radio prose is represented by stable string IDs, word counts, hashes and original voice/animation filenames rather than reproduced verbatim.

## Scope and verified totals

| Record type | Count |
| --- | --- |
| Campaign entries | 41 |
| Placed ship/object records | 1654 |
| Wing controllers | 361 |
| Mission events / SEXP programs | 2315 |
| Mission goals | 111 |
| Defined communications | 1287 |
| Resolved communication dispatch references | 1287 |
| Built-in/external communication dispatch references | 0 |
| Defined messages with no direct named dispatch | 14 |
| Defined messages with multiple dispatch sites | 14 |
| Waypoint paths | 157 |
| Callable reinforcement records | 10 |

The totals above are counted from parsed records, not from the `;! N total` comments written by FRED, because several source files contain stale editor counts. The object count is the number of object declarations, not the maximum simultaneous population: wing `$Waves`, thresholds, arrival cues and destroyed/departed state determine runtime concurrency. A selectable player ship may also be replaced by campaign loadout rules.

## Data authority, version and reconstruction rules

- **Mission baseline:** the single-player mission definitions and campaign graph in FreeSpace Upgrade MediaVPs 5.0.2 `MV_Assets.vp`, downloaded from the current FSNebula distribution. Package SHA-256: `8c89f1c2824518cf6b4c48f14ad10aa90b82867716fa610ec0669c4998661b76`. The package describes itself as containing upgraded models, maps and missions.

- **Campaign graph:** `FreeSpace2.fc2`, SHA-256 `1b770d6699da3a90b6bde9f6843b22084195026fd5e4115880f637cf2c6d3224`.

- **Retail caveat:** these are community-maintained MediaVP mission definitions, usually carrying the `FSU MEDIAVPS` AI profile and fixes made after 1999. They closely preserve the retail campaign but are not claimed to be byte-identical to retail 1.20. A legal retail `root_fs2.vp` can be diffed against the per-file hashes in this document for a strict retail audit.

- **Narrative handling:** mission titles, object names, event names and short UI labels are retained. Long original dialogue/briefing/debrief text is omitted. Each omitted record retains its `XSTR` ID, word count and a truncated SHA-256, so an owner of the game can verify or reconnect their local text without ambiguity.

- **Timing units:** ordinary SEXP delay operands and `+Chained` values are seconds unless the operator defines otherwise. `send-message-list` uses milliseconds after the previous message; the first entry is normally zero. Random-delay expressions such as `(rand 5 10)` remain nondeterministic.

- **Arrival/departure precedence:** ships in a wing use the wing controller's effective arrival/departure settings. Standalone objects use their own object-level cue. `(true)` is immediate once the mission/wing controller is active; `(false)` prevents independent arrival and is normal for wing-owned objects.

- **Faction notation:** `$Team` is the initial mission IFF, not always political allegiance. This matters in the undercover SOC loop. The manifest therefore keeps species/origin, inferred political role and initial IFF separately; all `change-iff` events are preserved in the exact event graph.

- **Source coordinate system:** object locations, 3×3 orientation matrices, waypoint vectors and briefing-camera coordinates are reproduced unchanged in the sanitized source for each mission.

- **Runtime dependencies not contained here:** ship/weapon physics, models, effects, built-in engine messages and UI behaviour come from global tables and engine code. This document captures every campaign mission reference to those systems, but a remake must independently implement or replace the global systems.

- **Duplicate message keys:** internal message names are not guaranteed unique inside a mission. Every definition is retained in file order; the sanitized source is authoritative where a name-based dispatch is ambiguous.

The first SOC offer follows `SM1-10`; accepting enters `Loop1-1` through `Loop1-3`, while declining proceeds to `SM2-01`. `Loop1-2` can also return early to the main campaign through its `Goto main campaign` event. The second offer follows `SM3-05`; accepting runs `Loop2-1` and `Loop2-2`, then rejoins at `SM3-06`.

## 02. Training 2 (`Training-2.fs2`)

**Training · Required · Aquitaine simulator**

Target-selection and weapons familiarisation: nearest-hostile and escort targeting, primary-bank linking, dumb-fire and homing secondaries, dual-fire, ammunition management, communications and calling a support ship.

## 04. Surrender, Belisarius! (`SM1-01.fs2`)

**Act I · Main · Deneb — Cygnus Prime**

The 53rd Hammerheads protect damaged Vasudan refugee transports until the GVD Psamtik can recover their passengers. NTF fighter waves and the cruiser Belisarius attack; mission progression requires Iota to survive.

## 05. The Place of Chariots (`SM1-02.fs2`)

**Act I · Main · Deneb asteroid belt**

The Hammerheads assault a concealed NTF installation. The apparent depot breaks apart to reveal the NTF Iceni; the command ship is scripted to escape, while the player suppresses its escort and installation defences.

## 06. The Romans Blunder (`SM1-03.fs2`)

**Act I · Main · Deneb–Sirius jump route**

Allied forces pursue Bosch and the Iceni toward the Sirius node. The player fights the covering force and logistics traffic; the campaign continues when the mission's May Continue event is satisfied.

## 09. A Lion at the Door (`SM1-04.fs2`)

**Act I · Main · Gamma Draconis node**

After a Shivan strike in Capella, the 107th Ravens secure the newly discovered Gamma Draconis portal and defend allied ships while the first major contact on this front develops.

## 10. Mystery of the Trinity (`SM1-05.fs2`)

**Act I · Main · Nebula beyond Gamma Draconis**

The Ravens follow Zeta through the nebula, locate the Trinity and protect the Discovery. The Trinity's loss to sustained Shivan attack is scripted; the player cannot save it in normal play.

## 11. The Great Hunt (`SM1-06.fs2`)

**Act I · Main · Nebula beyond Gamma Draconis**

The 107th joins the Actium and Lysander on a search-and-destroy sweep. Shivan forces escalate until the Ravana arrives; both allied corvettes are narratively doomed.

## 12. Slaying Ravana (`SM1-07.fs2`)

**Act I · Main · Nebula beyond Gamma Draconis**

A bomber strike led by the 107th destroys the Ravana. The mission is built around capital-ship subsystem attack, fighter cover and safe rearming near the Kehnmu.

## 14. The Sixth Wonder (`SM1-08.fs2`)

**Act I · Main · Epsilon Pegasi — Enif Station**

## 15. Into the Maelstrom (`SM1-09.fs2`)

**Act I · Main · Epsilon Pegasi asteroid field**

The 242nd escorts the Jooyun, Paracombe and Avila through an asteroid field to rendezvous with the Colossus. Bomber interception and disabling the Maelstrom's dangerous beam weapon are the critical tasks.

## 16. Feint! Parry! Riposte! (`SM1-10.fs2`)

**Act I · Main · Epsilon Pegasi**

The Suicide Kings attack rebel cruisers to draw the NTD Repulse into a trap. The Repulse's desperate collision course against the Colossus is a scripted set piece; this mission opens the first SOC offer.

**SOC Loop I · Optional · GTVA cargo depot**

## 20. Battle of the Wilderness (`SM2-01.fs2`)

**Act II · Main · Nebula beyond Gamma Draconis**

The 134th Barracudas escort the Vauban and Erinpura in the first operational deployment of the Lucidity AWACS platform. Long-range detection and spaced Shivan attacks define the mission.

## 22. Proving Grounds (`SM2-03.fs2`)

**Act II · Main · Nebula proving ground**

A two-part Pegasus exercise becomes a live Shivan engagement. Saving the Oberon in the stealth-fighter phase is optional; later, the Aquitaine needs targeting support against the Tiamat.

## 23. The King's Gambit (`SM2-04.fs2`)

**Act II · Main · Capella blockade route**

The 64th Raptors bomb NTF blockade-runners. Beam platforms assist against early warships, but the player must retain enough heavy ordnance to stop the late-arriving Perseverance.

## 25. Endgame (`SM2-06.fs2`)

**Act II · Main · Gamma Draconis — Knossos**

The NTF campaign reaches its end at Knossos. The Colossus is sabotaged and cannot stop Bosch; the Iceni's escape through the portal is scripted even though the surrounding rebel force can be defeated.

### Mission metadata

## 26. The Fog of War (`SM2-07.fs2`)

**Act II · Main · Nebula resource field**

The 203rd attacks a Shivan gas-mining operation and then protects the Tatenen. A Sathanas arrives, destroys the Tatenen by script and must be visually identified before withdrawal.

## 27. A Monster in the Mist (`SM2-08.fs2`)

**Act II · Main · Nebula**

Flying a Ptah, Alpha 1 scans the Sathanas's subsystems and may attack selected turrets. The reconnaissance craft is not intended for a stand-up fight; the juggernaut eventually departs.

## 29. A Flaming Sword (`SM2-10.fs2`)

**Act II · Main · Gamma Draconis — Knossos**

Three meson-bomb placements demolish Knossos as a last resort. Each placement is a timed escort problem; the player must protect the bombs and the Renenet and clear the blast zones.

## 30. Bearbaiting (`SM3-01.fs2`)

**Act III · Main · Gamma Draconis–Capella route**

The 203rd disables the Sathanas's four forward beam cannons before it reaches Capella. Flak suppression, repeated Helios strikes and timely rearming are central; the target then jumps onward.

## 32. Return to Babel (`SM3-03.fs2`)

**Act III · Main · Knossos/nebula route**

Allied forces catch the Iceni, but Bosch's contact with the Shivans changes the operation. The mission combines protection of the command ship with destruction of the Sammael and Azmedaj.

## 33. Straight, No Chaser (`SM3-04.fs2`)

**Act III · Main · Uncharted nebula**

## 34. Argonautica (`SM3-05.fs2`)

**Act III · Main · Nebula near Gamma Draconis node**

The 203rd protects the disabled Aquitaine, the Agrippa and repair assets while Shivan waves attack. Completion opens the second, optional SOC rescue loop.

**SOC Loop II · Optional · Nebula**

## 36. Into the Lion's Den (`Loop2-2.fs2`)

**SOC Loop II · Optional · Beyond the second Knossos**

Snipes leads a reconnaissance strike through the second portal. Alpha destroys the unknown subspace devices, observes the massed Shivan fleet and escapes through the node after engine recovery.

## 37. Exodus (`SM3-06.fs2`)

**Act III · Main · Capella**

Now leading the 70th Blue Lions, Alpha 1 escorts evacuation transports, the Vesalius and the Sulla. Bomber and bomb interception determine how much of the convoy survives.

## 39. Their Finest Hour (`SM3-08.fs2`)

**Act III · Main · Capella — Gamma Draconis node**

The Alliance stages a feint to buy evacuation time. The Colossus remains behind and is destroyed by Shivan juggernauts; the loss cannot be prevented through normal play.

## 41. Apocalypse (`SM3-10.fs2`)

**Act III · Main · Capella — Vega node**

The final red-alert mission covers allied withdrawal for roughly twelve minutes before Capella goes supernova. Escaping through the node and dying in the blast select different ending variants. The source calls this mission Apocalypse; some walkthroughs call it Incoming Transmission.

## Global implementation notes for a remake

1. **Implement FRED's event evaluator, not a fixed timeline.** Many apparent timestamps are conditional on destruction, docking, scanning, distance, subsystem state, previous events or random ranges. A cutscene-like linear playback will diverge quickly.

2. **Keep object declarations separate from wing controllers.** Wing-owned objects commonly have object-level false cues; spawning them from the object record instead of the wing cue will duplicate or prematurely reveal ships.

3. **Preserve event chaining.** A large share of dialogue pacing uses always-true events with `+Chained` offsets. The chain is part of mission logic even when the visible trigger is simply `(true)`.

4. **Model message queues and priorities.** `send-message-list` delays are relative to the previous item in milliseconds. Standard `send-message` events can still be delayed by their event trigger or chain. Persona and source selection affect the portrait/voice and whether an `<any wingman>` message has an eligible sender.

5. **Support scripted invulnerability/beam control.** `ship-guardian`, `ship-invulnerable`, `beam-free`, `beam-lock`, `turret-free`, `turret-lock`, tagged-only and subsystem-strength actions are essential to the campaign's famous set pieces.

6. **Treat impossible rescues and kills as design, not bugs.** Several losses/escapes are protected by guardianship, forced damage, timed beam fire, impossible distance or campaign events. The mission summaries flag the best-known examples; the event graph is definitive.

7. **Carry red-alert state.** `SM3-09` leads directly into `SM3-10`; surviving hull, wing state and eligible carried data must persist according to the engine's red-alert rules.

8. **Recreate global tables independently.** Mission files name ship classes, weapons, personas, music, nebulae, backgrounds, icons, models, sounds and cutscenes but do not define their global statistics. A legally clean remake needs new assets and independently specified physics/UI while resolving every named reference in this document.

## Sources and cross-checks

- [FSNebula — FreeSpace Upgrade MediaVPs 5.0.2](https://fsnebula.org/mod/MVPS): distribution and package descriptions; the extracted `MV_Assets.vp` is the primary mission-data source.

- [FreeSpace 2 mission-by-mission medal/walkthrough guide](https://www.nightsolo.net/games/fs2guide/missions.html): cross-check for public mission order, major scripted outcomes and medals.

- [FreeSpace Wiki — Mission Chatter](https://wiki.hard-light.net/index.php/Mission_Chatter): context for radio-message construction and pacing.

- [FreeSpace Wiki — What Makes a Good Mission?](https://wiki.hard-light.net/index.php/What_Makes_a_Good_Mission%3F): documents `send-message-list` fields and confirms that each delay is milliseconds after the previous message.

- [FRED2 editor documentation](https://fs2downloads.com/freddocs2/editors.html) and [advanced retail FRED help](https://www.fs2downloads.com/fredretail.html): editor semantics, arrival cues and SEXP-oriented mission construction.

- [FreeSpace 2 engine source repository](https://github.com/scp-fs2open/fs2open.github.com): authoritative implementation reference for parsing mission fields and executing SEXPs. The engine source is separate from the retail narrative/media data.

- [FreeSpace Wiki `tstrings.tbl` format](https://wiki.hard-light.net/index.php/Tstrings.tbl): explains the numeric localization IDs retained beside omitted narrative strings.

- [FreeSpace 2 overview](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FreeSpace_2): secondary cross-check for release, developer and broad campaign premise.
